money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: Iceland's currency is the Icelandic Kroner (ISK). Declare cash of over 10,000 euros or equivalent if you're travelling between Iceland and any non-EU country. This covers all forms of currency, not only cash. You'll have to pay a fine on entry or exit if you: don't declare your money give incorrect information You can use major credit cards in most places.

laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences, even for possession of small amounts of recreational drugs or some prescription medications, include: heavy fines imprisonment being removed from the Schengen area a potential entry ban If you intend to take medication, confirm it's legal in your destination. Check if any rules or restrictions apply. Depending on your medication, you may need to apply for a permit to bring it to your destination. Always carry a copy of your prescription and transport your medication in its original container.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Always carry an ID, such as your driver's licence or a copy of your passport. Penalties for drink driving and speeding are severe and include the following: heavy fines jail sentences Even minor offences can attract fines and jail sentences. If you're found guilty of an offence: you may face jail or deportation you may be banned from the Schengen area
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: Australian driving licences are valid in Iceland if you have had your licence for a minimum of 1 year. However, some car rental companies require customers to present an International Driving Permit (IDP) if holding a licence issued outside Europe or North America. Digital driver's licences may not be accepted. If you need an IDP, get this before you leave Australia. An IDP doesn't replace the requirement for a regular driver's license. visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Visa-free short stays (90 days or less) as part of the Schengen area, in some cases.
visa-preparation.before_departure: Nothing to lodge before travel today: EES registration happens at the border. ETIAS hadn't started on 2026-11-01.
steps: Iceland is in the Schengen area: short stays of 90 days or less can be visa-free in some cases; other purposes or longer stays need a visa before travel.
At the first Schengen border, give fingerprints and a photo for the Entry/Exit System (EES). It's free; nothing is needed before arrival, and sites charging for it are fraudulent.
Carry your passport when crossing borders, including inside Schengen (temporary internal checks are in place in places).
